claims.text: For all encounters, the intervention integrating machine learning mortality predictions with behavioral nudges increased serious illness conversation rates from 1.3% in the control group to 4.6% in the intervention group (adjusted difference in percentage points, 3.3; 95% CI, 2.3-4.5; P < .001).

Among high-risk patient encounters, the intervention increased serious illness conversation rates from 3.6% in the control group to 15.2% in the intervention group (adjusted difference in percentage points, 11.6; 95% CI, 8.2-12.5; P < .001).

For all encounters, advance care planning conversations were conducted in 1.9% of control encounters compared with 4.9% of intervention encounters (adjusted difference in percentage points, 3.0; 95% CI, 2.1-4.1; P = .001).

Among high-risk patient encounters, advance care planning conversations were conducted in 5.8% of control encounters compared with 17.5% of intervention encounters (adjusted difference in percentage points, 11.7; 95% CI, 8.4-15.7; P < .001).
The intervention produced an off-target increase of nearly 2 percentage points in serious illness conversations among patients who were not classified as high risk by the algorithm.
Oncologists correctly identify fewer than half of their patients who will die within 6 to 12 months.

evidence.description: Among all patients, SICs were conducted in 155 of 12 170 control encounters (1.3%) and 632 of 13 889 intervention encounters (4.6%). In adjusted analyses of all patients, the intervention led to a significant increase in the SIC rate (adjusted difference in percentage points, 3.3; 95% CI, 2.3-4.5; P < .001).

Among high-risk patients, SICs were conducted in 77 of 2125 control encounters (3.6%) and 304 of 1999 intervention encounters (15.2%). In adjusted analyses of 4124 high-risk patient encounters, there was a significant increase in the SIC rate (adjusted difference in percentage points, 11.6; 95% CI, 8.2-12.5; P < .001).

Among all patients, ACPs were conducted in 231 of 12 170 control encounters (1.9%) and 680 of 13 889 intervention encounters (4.9%). In adjusted analyses of all patients, the intervention led to a significant increase in the ACP rate (adjusted difference in percentage points, 3.0; 95% CI, 2.1-4.1; P = .001).

Among high-risk patients, ACPs were conducted in 124 of 2125 control encounters (5.8%) and 350 of 1999 intervention encounters (17.5%). In adjusted analyses of high-risk patients, the intervention led to a significant increase in the ACP rate (adjusted difference in percentage points, 11.7; 95% CI, 8.4-15.7; P < .001).

Although our intervention effect was strongest in the high-risk patients flagged by the algorithm, we still detected an increase of nearly 2 percentage points in SICs among patients who were not deemed high-risk by the algorithm.
Citing references 11 and 12: 'First, oncologists correctly identify fewer than half of their patients who will die within 6 to 12 months.'

methodologies.name: Stepped-wedge cluster randomized clinical trial of machine learning mortality predictions combined with behavioral nudges
methodologies.description: Evaluated a multimodal clinician-directed intervention consisting of weekly performance feedback with peer comparisons, EHR dashboard lists of high-risk 180-day mortality patients identified by an ML algorithm, and appointment-day opt-out text reminders across 5 four-week wedges.
datasets: University of Pennsylvania Health System electronic health record data
conditions: 9 medical oncology clinics grouped into 8 clinic groups
High-risk defined as >=10% predicted 180-day mortality risk
Up to 6 high-risk patients listed per clinician per week

limitations.text: The study was conducted within a single academic health system, and the participants may not be representative of the general population of oncologists or patients with cancer.
Early advance care planning and serious illness conversations were evaluated as surrogate measures rather than longer-term patient clinical or quality-of-life outcomes.
The multicomponent nature of the intervention prevents disentangling the specific effects of individual components such as peer comparisons, high-risk lists, or opt-out text messages.

Oncologists correctly identify fewer than half of their patients who will die within 6 to 12 months, leading to overoptimistic assessments of short-term mortality risk and inadequate identification of patients needing timely discussions.

future_work.text: Conduct longer-term studies to determine clinical and quality-of-life outcomes associated with serious illness conversations prompted by algorithm-based interventions.
Use head-to-head comparisons to determine which specific intervention components deliver the most benefit.
Evaluate how an integrated EHR-based mortality prediction tool can be generalized to other health systems.
